svg.title: Relay neuron (interneuron)
svg.desc: A multipolar relay neuron inside the spinal cord: many branched dendrites receiving synapses from sensory neurons, a cell body with nucleus, an axon hillock, and a short unmyelinated axon branching into terminals that end in synaptic knobs.

g.data-name: Grey matter of the spinal cord (CNS)
g.data-info: Relay neurons lie entirely within the brain and spinal cord, linking sensory and motor neurons.
g.aria-label: Grey matter of the spinal cord (CNS)

g.data-info: Many short, branched dendrites receive signals at synapses from sensory neurons (and other neurons).
Contains the nucleus; integrates the excitatory and inhibitory signals arriving from many synapses.
Where the summed potentials decide whether an action potential starts.
Short axon with no myelin. The action potential travels continuously along the whole membrane, so conduction is slower than in a myelinated fibre; over short distances in the CNS this is fast enough.
Branches of the axon that pass the signal to several other neurons, e.g. motor neurons.
Release neurotransmitter onto the next neuron (for example a motor neuron in a reflex arc).
Contains the DNA; large and central.
Makes ribosomes for the protein synthesis the neuron needs.
Synaptic knob of a sensory neuron ending on a dendrite of the relay neuron.

g.text: Grey matter of the spinal cord (CNS)

svg.text: No myelin: the impulse moves continuously along the axon (compare the jumping, saltatory conduction of the motor neuron).
